summary: Reuses an existing code-execution sandbox instead of getting a fresh one. Every request that runs code gets a container; passing its id back keeps the same filesystem alive, so files written on one turn are still there on the next.
combines: Only relevant alongside the code execution tool. Without that tool there is no container to reuse.
The response carries a top-level container object with its id and an expires_at timestamp; that id is what you send back.

A container is checkpointed after roughly five minutes idle and restored on the next request. It expires 30 days after creation, and an expired id cannot be reused: drop the parameter to get a new one.
The rolling expires_at in the response is shorter than the real 30-day limit, so it is not a reliable signal of when the container is gone for good.
It can also carry a skills list, capped at 20 entries.
Lixpi does not run the code execution tool today, so this has nothing to attach to yet.
